title: When the Promise Turns
premise: Marine biologist Isandro Vasquez has spent three years in the small coastal town of Punta Clara rebuilding after a betrayal that cost him his research post and his faith in love, counting sea turtles instead of heartbreaks. When his sister's wedding forces him home, he recruits Wren Okafor—a sharp-tongued marine veterinarian he's secretly admired for months—to pose as his partner for one weekend. The fake date turns devastatingly real by dessert, but Wren is offered a dream fellowship abroad the same week Isandro's restored turtle sanctuary finally wins permanent funding that requires him to stay. As secrets about why Isandro really left his old life surface, both must decide whether loyalty to the versions of themselves they built alone matters more than the truth of what they've become together. In the end, they choose a third path: Wren defers the fellowship a year to work alongside him at the sanctuary, proving that love against duty doesn't have to mean losing either.
about_author: X. M. Voss is a former field researcher who traded tide charts for typewriters and now writes love stories set where the land meets the sea. They live in a coastal town much like Punta Clara with two rescue dogs and an unreasonable number of houseplants.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Three years into his quiet life at Punta Clara's turtle sanctuary, Isandro has perfected the art of small safe steps—until his sister Marisol calls with wedding invitations and pointed questions about his plus-one. He panics and lies, claiming he's seeing someone. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of avoidance cracking under family pressure.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Fixes Broken Things
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Marine veterinarian Wren Okafor arrives to treat an injured loggerhead, all dry wit and steady hands, and Isandro realizes she's the only person in town who might agree to a ridiculous favor. Over bad coffee, he asks her to be his fake date. She laughs—then says yes, for reasons she doesn't examine too closely. Beat: reluctant hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They negotiate terms over tacos: no real feelings, no real names of exes, exit anytime. Wren notices how carefully Isandro deflects every personal question; Isandro notices how easily she makes him laugh. A shared moment tending the injured turtle hints at deeper compatibility. Beat: chemistry establishing itself despite the contract.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Vasquez family reunion begins—loud, warm, suffocating. Wren watches Isandro shrink inside his own history and starts piecing together the story he won't tell: a disgraced mentor, stolen research, a career destroyed by misplaced loyalty. His mother pulls Wren aside with a knowing look. Beat: found family beginning to claim her.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During the rehearsal dinner toast, Marisol ambushes them with affection, and improvising together, Isandro and Wren build a history so convincing it frightens him. On the porch afterward, almost-kiss interrupted by a call: Wren has been offered the fellowship in Lisbon. Beat: desire colliding with consequence.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings In
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Back at the sanctuary, they fall into effortless partnership rescuing a nest after a storm, working hip to hip through the night. Wren admits she wants the fellowship—and wants him. Isandro, terrified of wanting anything, pulls back coldly. Beat: first real wound, self-inflicted.

chapters.title: The Truth About Loyalty
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Marisol confronts him: she knows the fake-dating secret and demands the truth about the old scandal. He confesses—he covered for his mentor's fraud to protect the lab team, and lost everything for loyalty that was never returned. Wren overhears. Beat: the lie beneath the lie exposed; trust shattered on the eve of the wedding.

chapters.title: Vows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wedding day. Isandro performs happiness while Wren decides whether Lisbon is escape or answer. During the vows, watching Marisol choose boldly, Wren understands she can't defer her own life—or her feelings. She finds Isandro alone and tells him the fake part ended weeks ago. Beat: confession without guarantee.

chapters.title: When the Promise Turns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. The sanctuary's funding board offers Isandro permanence—but only if he commits fully, publicly, staying put. Wren's Lisbon deadline lands the same day. Cornered by both futures, Isandro nearly repeats his old pattern, sacrificing himself silently. Instead, he chooses honesty: he asks her to stay, not as a favor, but as a choice. Beat: love against duty, refusing false binaries.

chapters.title: A Year of Small Brave Steps
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Six months later: Wren has deferred Lisbon one year to co-lead the sanctuary's new veterinary program, their application approved as a joint project. At the season's first nest hatchling release, surrounded by chosen family, they watch tiny turtles race toward a vast uncertain ocean—and follow them. Beat: resolution; safety redefined as courage shared.
